title: for every substitution-span gate that survives E318's count-word prune, is the gated quantity itself published in the block, and what ambiguity remains?

join_rules.population: E317's substitution-span leaves (a block publishing >= 2 positive numeric candidates) minus the leaves E318 pruned as counts
join_rules.candidates: positive numeric leaves of the gate's own block, excluding tolerance-named and noise-named leaves and the gate leaf itself -- the rule that published E317's span
join_rules.name_token: the gate's own key, tolerance word removed (close_diff_tolerance -> close+diff); when the key carries nothing else the block's name is used and that is published as the source
join_rules.magnitude_fingerprint: a candidate equal to the gate value at 1e-12 relative: the same number printed twice
join_rules.classes: resolved_by_name / resolved_by_copy (exactly one identification) / ambiguous (>= 2 identifications) / unresolved (none) / block or face unreadable

notes: 23 of 219 gates are avoidable by a reader who reads the whole block (16 by the quantity's own name token, 7 by the gate's magnitude printed twice); 134 are not.
E317's substitution span is a worst case for the reader who stops at the first number: after the identified candidate is removed the median span falls from 1.979 to 1.347 decades.

the quantity's name comes from the gate's own key on 108 rows; on 96 rows the key names nothing but the tolerance word and on 15 it names only a unit, so those rows are resolved by the fingerprint channel or not at all.
a resolved row is not a readable gate: E317 already measured that 33 of 1108 leaves are reader-complete, and resolving the quantity does not supply the unit.
